episodes.title: Introduction to Historical Thinking
episodes.description: Introduce history as an investigation of causes, events, and their continuing significance.

episodes.title: Southwest Borderlands
episodes.description: In this episode, we dive into the Hohokam and Ancestral Puebloans of the Southwest Borderlands, two indigenous cultures that had tremendous impact on these lands.

episodes.title: Southeast and Plains
episodes.description: The Mississippian Culture was a Native American civilization that thrived in what is now known as the American Southeast.

episodes.title: Northeast Region
episodes.description: In this episode, we discuss the establishment of the Iroquois Confederacy and the indigenous people that continue to call the Northeast region home today.

episodes.title: West Africa and Western Europe
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge dives into West Africa and Western Europe and discusses the ways they created a distinctly unique, American culture.

episodes.title: French and Dutch Colonies
episodes.description: While English colonies get all of the credit, Dutch and French colonies played a big role in shaping American culture.

episodes.title: Early Spanish and English Colonization
episodes.description: Like the English, the Spanish wished to find wealth and spread Christianity but their approach to colonization was different.

episodes.title: Puritans & Pilgrims in New England
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses Puritans, Pilgrims, and the New England colonies' impact on Indigenous cultures.

episodes.title: England's Growing Empire
episodes.description: Explore how sugar production and natural disasters shaped colonial history.

episodes.title: Proprietary Colonies
episodes.description: Explore the development of proprietary colonies in North America.

episodes.title: Rebellions
episodes.description: Examine resistance to colonial authority, including violence and rebellion.

episodes.title: Power, Enslavement, and Resistance
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses how enslavers stayed in power for over two centuries, as well as how the enslaved resisted that power.

episodes.title: Indigenous Power
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses Native American culture, influence, and power in the 18th Century and the ways in which Indigenous peoples interacted with Europeans.

episodes.title: Anglicization, Enlightenment, and Republicanism
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses the Enlightenment, its positives and negatives, and the ways in which this period shaped our present.

episodes.title: Imperial Wars, Imperial Crisis
episodes.description: Explore the Seven Years' War and its consequences for colonies, territory, and power in North America.

episodes.title: The American Revolution
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses the events that lead to and transpired during the American Revolution.

episodes.title: Articles of Confederation and Constitution
episodes.description: Explore the Articles of Confederation, their relationship to the Constitution, and state constitutions in the early United States.

episodes.title: The New Nation in the World
episodes.description: In this episode, we discuss the events that led to creating the political and cultural foundations on which the new nation would stand.

episodes.title: Life In the New Nation
episodes.description: Explore how historians study everyday life in early America and what they can learn about the people who lived there.

episodes.title: Slavery, Freedom, Resistance
episodes.description: Explore the lives of enslaved people in nineteenth-century America, including their survival, resistance, and experiences of freedom.

episodes.title: Growth, Conquest, War
episodes.description: Explore how nineteenth-century growth, conquest, and war transformed the United States.

episodes.title: Capitalism in Early America
episodes.description: Trace the shift from local exchange to a market society and examine capitalism’s influence on American culture.

episodes.title: Politics and Print
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses the changes that were happening in American politics during the 1820s and ‘30s and the influence transportation and communication had over these.

episodes.title: Religion in the New Nation
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses the ways religion influenced life in early America.

episodes.title: German and Irish Immigration
episodes.description: Explore nineteenth-century Irish and German immigration to the United States and how immigrants were treated.

episodes.title: Going West, Facing East
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses Westward Expansion and the impact it had on communities and nations throughout the continent.

episodes.title: Crisis Approaches
episodes.description: Examine the Fugitive Slave Act, the Republican Party’s founding, and Bleeding Kansas as turning points toward the Civil War.

episodes.title: Crisis, Secession, and War
episodes.description: Trace escalating conflicts over slavery, from Dred Scott to secession and civil war.

episodes.title: Civil War, Pt. 1: Causes and Battles
episodes.description: Danielle Bainbridge discusses the reasons for secession and key battles of the American Civil War.

episodes.title: Civil War, Pt.2: Victory and Unfinished Victory
episodes.description: Examine unresolved questions after the Civil War and consider how historical understanding can inform the present.
